description_full: SITC International Holdings Company Limited, a shipping logistics company, engages in the provision of integrated transportation and logistics solutions in Mainland China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan, Southeast Asia, and internationally. The company offers container transportation, freight forwarding, shipping agency, depot, warehousing services, container vessel leasing, land leasing, and other services. As of December 31, 2024, the company operated a fleet of 114 vessels with a total capacity of 180,255 TEU, including 100 self-owned vessels with a capacity of 164,845 TEU and 14 chartered vessels with a capacity of 15,410 TEU. It also provides vessel holding and chartering, technology support, container marine transportation, container maintenance, customs declaration, marine, shipping management, and multimodal transportation services, as well as engages in the land and building holding activities. SITC International Holdings Company Limited was founded in 1991 and is headquartered in Wan Chai, Hong Kong.

financial_summary: SITC INTERNATIONAL HLDGS CO LTD is a large-cap industrials business with a $18.3B market cap on $3.4B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -6% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are contracting by -3.4pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 54% against a 9% cost of capital — a 45-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 38%.

The business throws off $1.3B in free cash flow — roughly 37 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.15× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 75× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 5.1% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 49% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 3.1× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
